answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any supplier transition (switch_primary_vendor or add_second_source) carries acute delivery-risk exposure that the current situation cannot absorb. Memory_c2's cost win from switching vendors is a single archived instance whose onboarding conditions (no line pressure, presumably more lead time) don't match today's tight 14-day window, so I want to verify its original context before trusting it as a template. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal with the incumbent recovered real margin via market benchmarking without any migration risk, and memory_c6 corroborates that multi-year/volume commitments with the same incumbent cut unit cost without narrowing scope — together these directly address the 18% spend-cut mandate while preserving the delivery continuity memory_c1 also associates with the incumbent relationship. I'm verifying memory_c4 and memory_c2 specifically to confirm the negotiated outcome was durable and to check whether the switch-vendor case involved buffer/slack conditions absent here before ruling it out. Given only one sourcing move is available this cycle, negotiating terms with the incumbent best minimizes total cost of ownership without increasing delivery risk, leaving switch/second-source options for a future cycle once there's more schedule slack to absorb transition risk.
